tool.name: Savont ASV
tool.description: Generate amplicon sequence variants (ASVs) from long-read amplicon sequences
tool.command: #import re #if str($input_mode.mode) == "single" #set $reads_list = [$input_mode.reads] #else #set $reads_list = $input_mode.reads #end if #for $read in $reads_list #set $safe_name = re.sub('[^\w\-_\.]', '_', str($read.element_identifier)) ln -sf '$read' "$safe_name" && #end for savont asv #for $read in $reads_list #set $safe_name = re.sub('[^\w\-_\.]', '_', str($read.element_identifier)) "$safe_name" #end for -o 'savont_out' -t "\${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1}" --log-level $general.log_level $general.no_band #if str($amplicon_preset.preset) == "hifi" --hifi #end if #if str($amplicon_preset.preset) == "rrna_operon" --rrna-operon #end if #if str($amplicon_preset.preset) == "custom" --min-read-length $amplicon_preset.min_read_length --max-read-length $amplicon_preset.max_read_length #end if #if str($amplicon_preset.preset) != "hifi" --min-cluster-size $amplicon_preset.min_cluster_size #end if #if str($input_mode.mode) == "joint" and str($input_mode.pooled_samples) not in ("", "false", "False") --pooled-samples #end if --quality-value-cutoff $io.quality_value_cutoff --minimum-base-quality $io.minimum_base_quality $clustering.single_strand --n-depth-cutoff $consensus.n_depth_cutoff $consensus.use_hpc $consensus.mask_low_quality --posterior-threshold-ln $consensus.posterior_threshold_ln $consensus.low_polymorphism --chimera-allowable-errors $chimera.chimera_allowable_errors #if $chimera.chimera_detect_length --chimera-detect-length $chimera.chimera_detect_length #end if && cp savont_out/savont_*.log '$output_log'

param.name: reads
param.label: Input amplicon sequences
param.help: A FASTQ or FASTA file (optionally gzipped) containing full-length amplicon reads with >98% base accuracy, e.g. from ONT R10.4.1 or PacBio HiFi sequencing.

param.name: reads
param.label: Input amplicon sequences
param.help: Two or more FASTQ or FASTA files (optionally gzipped) containing full-length amplicon reads with >98% base accuracy, e.g. from ONT R10.4.1 or PacBio HiFi sequencing. The files are concatenated into one sample unless 'Treat each input file as a separate sample' is checked.

param.name: pooled_samples
param.label: Treat each input file as a separate sample
param.help: Pool all reads together for ASV detection but quantify each input file separately, producing one feature table column per input file. Leave unchecked to concatenate all input files into a single sample.

param.name: min_read_length
param.label: Minimum read length
param.help: Reads shorter than this are discarded.

param.name: max_read_length
param.label: Maximum read length
param.help: Reads longer than this are discarded.

param.name: log_level
param.label: Logging verbosity level
param.help: Controls how much detail is written to the output log.

param.name: no_band
param.label: Use exact (unbanded) POA alignment
param.help: Slower, but better handles highly variable clusters.

param.name: quality_value_cutoff
param.label: Minimum estimated read accuracy
param.help: Reads whose estimated per-base accuracy is below this percentage are discarded.

param.name: minimum_base_quality
param.label: Minimum base quality
param.help: Bases with a quality score below this Phred value are masked. Set lower for older reads.

param.name: single_strand
param.label: Input reads are single-stranded
param.help: Use only forward strand k-mers (for strand-specific protocols).

param.name: n_depth_cutoff
param.label: Minimum depth for ambiguous sites
param.help: A site with more than one base is only resolved when the total depth exceeds this value.

param.name: use_hpc
param.label: Use homopolymer compression
param.help: Speeds up the clustering, useful for complex eukaryotic genomes.

param.name: mask_low_quality
param.label: Mask low-quality bases in the consensus
param.help: Mask (instead of resolving) low-quality sites in the consensus sequence.

param.name: posterior_threshold_ln
param.label: Negative alternate posterior probability threshold (natural log scale)
param.help: Higher values are more stringent for low-quality consensuses. Do not set higher than min_depth * ln(error_rate).

param.name: low_polymorphism
param.label: Expect low polymorphism in the sample
param.help: Skips SNPmer clustering and maps reads to ASVs with minimap2 instead (e.g. single-strain samples).

param.name: chimera_allowable_errors
param.label: Allowable errors for bi-chimeric detection
param.help: Higher values are more sensitive, but may filter out true ASVs.

param.name: chimera_detect_length
param.label: Length of near-perfect ASV segment matches
param.help: Higher values are less sensitive. By default this is 1/10 of the minimum read length.

tool.help:
**Savont ASV** turns high-accuracy long-read amplicon sequences (ONT R10.4.1 or PacBio HiFi) into Amplicon Sequence Variants (ASVs) at single-nucleotide resolution.
The tool builds a k-mer (SNPmer) index of the input reads, clusters reads that differ only by sequencing errors, resolves a consensus sequence for every cluster with an EM-based refinement, and finally dereplicates the consensus sequences.
Inputs ------
* **Input mode**: select *Batch processing* for a single input file (one sample), or *Joint processing* to supply several files at once. In joint mode the files are either concatenated into a single sample (default) or quantified separately, one feature table column per file (*Treat each input file as a separate sample*). * **Input amplicon sequences**: full-length amplicon reads in FASTQ or FASTA format. For 16S rRNA data, use the complete gene (about 1500 bp). * **Amplicon type**: selects sensible default read-length and clustering parameters. The PacBio HiFi option activates the ``--hifi`` preset, which lowers the minimum cluster size to 4 (HiFi reads have a lower error rate).
Outputs -------
* **ASVs**: representative consensus sequences. * **Feature table**: QIIME2-compatible tabular count table, one column per sample. * **Read assignments**: per-read assignment to an ASV with the estimated alignment identity. * **Log**: the full Savont run log.
Next steps ----------
The ASVs and feature table can be passed to **Savont classify** or **Savont SINTAX** for taxonomic profiling, or to **Savont export** to merge the results of several samples.
Note that Savont expects reads with a base accuracy of at least 98%; standard short-read (Illumina) data is **not** a suitable input for this tool.
